definition.given: The file contains more Waypoint layers than fit in the visible Layers panel. Layer-name search is open at the first matching result.
definition.observed: Clicking Previous changes the counter to 40 / 40 and selects Waypoint 40. The workspace shifts upward, moving the header and toolbar out of view and leaving empty space below the canvas.
definition.require: Navigating to the last search result brings the target layer into view while keeping the workspace header and toolbar visible and the canvas filling the available workspace area.
allow: The Layers list may scroll and the canvas may pan or animate to reveal the target.
Panel dimensions, spacing, and styling may vary while preserving access to the workspace controls.

theory.title: Jump to Item - Reveal a distant layer within the existing workspace
theory.reference: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition, Chapter 7: Lists of Things; designing-interfaces/chapters/ch07-lists.md
theory.rationale: Search navigation brings a distant layer into view within a long list. Keeping the surrounding workspace controls accessible lets the user continue working with that layer.

reference_observation: Clicking Previous selects Waypoint 40 while the workspace header and toolbar remain visible and the canvas continues to fill the available workspace area.
requirement_rationale: Layers represent the objects in a design file. When the list is too long to browse easily, search helps a designer locate an object to work on. Navigating to a result should scroll the layer list without displacing the canvas or hiding the editing controls.
